question: Can a spatial basis learned only from wave+Gray training patches replace the full raw 3x3 stencil while preserving transfer to unseen NLS and advection?

learned_spatial_basis.source: raw physical 3x3 patches from the same wave+Gray training trajectories used to fit the representation
learned_spatial_basis.method: separate per-channel PCA/eigendecomposition of centered 9-dimensional patch covariance
learned_spatial_basis.determinism: eigenvalues sorted descending; each eigenvector sign canonicalized by forcing its largest-magnitude coefficient positive

identifier.features: constant + 5 learned 3x3 patch projections for channel 0 + 5 learned projections for channel 1 + seven degree-2/3 center monomials

frozen_pass_rule: PASS only if every one of 3 fresh registered replicates has companded rollout MSE / raw-state persistence MSE < 1.0 on all 15 splits (45/45 cells). Any single cell >= 1.0 makes Phase 18 FAIL. No retry or replacement of a consumed replicate.
diagnostics: per-channel PCA explained variance for 5 components
raw full-stencil Phase-17 rollout control where practical
claim_limit: A pass would show that a compact spatial basis learned from seen training families can support transfer to two unseen synthetic law families. It would not establish unrestricted operator discovery or novel physics; locality, patch size, PCA rank, polynomial order, topology, and simulator families remain hand-specified.
